This appendix separates the contribution of the group sizes from that of the variances in the
denominator degrees of freedom of Welch's ANOVA, in balanced and in unbalanced designs.

Throughout, $k$ is the number of groups, $i = 1,\dots,k$ the group index, $n_i$ the size of
group $i$ and $\sigma_i^2$ its population variance. The denominator degrees of freedom of
Eq. \@ref(eq:welch-f), as returned by `oneway.test()`, are

\begin{equation}
\nu = \frac{k^{2}-1}
{3\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{k}\dfrac{\left(1-w_i/w\right)^{2}}{n_i-1}},
\qquad w_i = \frac{n_i}{s_i^{2}}, \quad w = \sum_{i=1}^{k} w_i .
(\#eq:welch-anova-df)
\end{equation}

The quantity examined here is Eq. \@ref(eq:welch-anova-df) with each $s_i^2$ replaced by
$\sigma_i^2$, which is fixed by the design $(n_i, \sigma_i)$ alone and therefore comparable across
configurations, whereas the computed value varies from replication to replication. No claim is
made below about how closely the computed value tracks it at small $n_i$.

# Separating the group sizes from the variances

Let $\bar n = k^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{k} n_i$ denote the mean group size and write

\begin{equation}
n_i = c_i\,\bar n, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^{k} c_i = k ,
(\#eq:size-proportions)
\end{equation}

with design constants $c_i$ fixing the shape of the size vector while $\bar n$ carries its scale.
In the simulations of Section \@ref(sec:simulation-results),
$\mathbf c = (0.5,\,0.8,\,1.2,\,1.5)$ for the unbalanced designs and $\mathbf c = (1,1,1,1)$ for
the balanced ones.

Substituting Eq. \@ref(eq:size-proportions) into the weights of Eq. \@ref(eq:welch-anova-df), the
factor $\bar n$ appears in $w_i$ and in $w$ alike and cancels in their ratio, so that the
normalised weights

\begin{equation}
u_i = \frac{w_i}{w} = \frac{c_i/\sigma_i^{2}}{\displaystyle\sum_{j=1}^{k} c_j/\sigma_j^{2}},
\qquad \sum_{i=1}^{k} u_i = 1 ,
(\#eq:normalised-weights)
\end{equation}

depend on the variances and on the shape of the size vector, but not on $\bar n$. With
Eq. \@ref(eq:normalised-weights),

\begin{equation}
\nu = \frac{k^{2}-1}
{3\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{k}\dfrac{(1-u_i)^{2}}{c_i\bar n-1}} ,
(\#eq:nu-exact)
\end{equation}

exactly. The mean group size now enters only through the denominators $c_i\bar n - 1$.

# Balanced designs

For $c_i = 1$, $i = 1,\dots,k$, every denominator term of Eq. \@ref(eq:nu-exact) carries the same
factor $\bar n - 1$, which can therefore be taken out of the sum. Writing

\begin{equation}
D = \frac{k^{2}-1}{3\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{k}\dfrac{(1-u_i)^{2}}{c_i}} ,
(\#eq:leading-factor)
\end{equation}

which does not depend on $\bar n$, Eq. \@ref(eq:nu-exact) becomes

\begin{equation}
\nu = D\,(\bar n - 1) .
(\#eq:nu-balanced)
\end{equation}

# Unbalanced designs

For general $c_i$ write $c_i\bar n - 1 = c_i\bar n\left(1 - (c_i\bar n)^{-1}\right)$ and expand
the reciprocal as a geometric series in $(c_i\bar n)^{-1}$, which converges provided

\begin{equation}
c_i\,\bar n > 1 \qquad \text{for all } i = 1,\dots,k .
(\#eq:expansion-condition)
\end{equation}

In the simulated designs $\min_i c_i = 0.5$, so Eq. \@ref(eq:expansion-condition) holds from
$\bar n = 3$ on. The sum in Eq. \@ref(eq:nu-exact) becomes

\begin{equation}
\sum_{i=1}^{k}\frac{(1-u_i)^{2}}{c_i\bar n-1}
= \frac{1}{\bar n}\sum_{i=1}^{k}\frac{(1-u_i)^{2}}{c_i}
  \left(1+\frac{1}{c_i\bar n}+O(\bar n^{-2})\right)
= \frac{1}{\bar n}\left(\frac{k^{2}-1}{3D} + \frac{E}{\bar n} + O(\bar n^{-2})\right),
(\#eq:denominator-expansion)
\end{equation}

with $D$ from Eq. \@ref(eq:leading-factor) and

\begin{equation}
E = \sum_{i=1}^{k}\frac{(1-u_i)^{2}}{c_i^{2}} .
(\#eq:second-moment)
\end{equation}

Inserting Eq. \@ref(eq:denominator-expansion) into Eq. \@ref(eq:nu-exact) and expanding the
reciprocal once more gives

\begin{equation}
\nu = D\,\bar n \;-\; \frac{3D^{2}E}{k^{2}-1} \;+\; O(\bar n^{-1}) .
(\#eq:nu-expansion)
\end{equation}

Eq. \@ref(eq:nu-balanced) is the special case $c_i \equiv 1$, for which $E = (k^{2}-1)/(3D)$ and
the constant term reduces to $D$.

# The ordering of the two influences

The variances enter Eq. \@ref(eq:nu-expansion) only through $D$, which contains no $\bar n$. Since
$\sum_i u_i = 1$ gives $\sum_i (1-u_i) = k-1$, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality in the form
$\left(\sum_i a_i\right)^{2} \le \left(\sum_i a_i^{2}/c_i\right)\left(\sum_i c_i\right)$ applied
to $a_i = 1-u_i$ yields

\begin{equation}
\sum_{i=1}^{k}\frac{(1-u_i)^{2}}{c_i} \;\ge\; \frac{(k-1)^{2}}{k} ,
(\#eq:cauchy-schwarz)
\end{equation}

with equality if and only if $(1-u_i)/c_i$ is constant in $i$, which holds in particular for a
balanced design with equal variances. In the opposite extreme one weight tends to one and the
others to zero, so that $\sum_i (1-u_i)^{2}/c_i \to \sum_{i \ne j} 1/c_i$. Hence

\begin{equation}
\frac{k^{2}-1}{3\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{k} 1/c_i} \;\le\; D \;\le\; \frac{k(k+1)}{3(k-1)} .
(\#eq:D-bounds)
\end{equation}

The two contributions are thus of different kind. The group sizes enter as an unbounded scale,

\begin{equation}
\lim_{\bar n \to \infty} \frac{\nu}{\bar n} = D ,
(\#eq:size-contribution)
\end{equation}

by Eq. \@ref(eq:nu-expansion), whereas the variances enter only through $D$, confined by
Eq. \@ref(eq:D-bounds) to a fixed interval whose upper end is attained under homoscedasticity in a
balanced design. No configuration of $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_k$ prevents $\nu$ from growing
proportionally to $\bar n$.
